title: Our Father! Through the Coming Year
description: Our Father! Through the Coming Year in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 390, “A New Year”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Our Fa-ther! through the com-ing year We know not what shall be, But we would leave with-out a fear Its or-dering all to Thee.

lines: Our Father! through the coming year
We know not what shall be,
But we would leave without a fear
Its ordering all to Thee.
It may be we shall toil in vain
For what the world holds fair,
And all its good we thought to gain
Deceive, and prove but care.
It may be it shall darkly blend
Our love with anxious fears,
And snatch away the valued friend,
The tried of many years.
It may be it shall bring us days
And nights of lingering pain,
And bid us take our farewell gaze
Of these loved haunts of men.
But calmly, Lord, on Thee we rest;
No fears our trust shall move;
Thou knowest what for each is best,
And Thou art perfect love.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
